title: Replication Codebase: Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade
description:
Clean, reproducible Python analytical and econometric codebase for the study: "Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade" (submitted to Nature Sustainability).

This archive contains exclusively the 13 core analytical Python modules (01–13) used to generate the empirical estimates, bioeconomic models, and optimization solutions reported in the manuscript: species-to-HS6 conservation concordances, Taxonomic Aggregation Ratio (TAR) and Species Customs Resolution Index (SCRI) audits, WCO HS 2028 legal amendment verification, Dual-IV scarcity pricing and wild-versus-farmed price tests, coupled wild-aquaculture differential-equation bifurcations and Pontryagin stochastic optimal control, Comparative Interrupted Time Series and zero-retaining Structural Gravity PPML estimations, bilateral mirror evasion and Stackelberg border inspection models, live-weight-equivalent marine trophic accounting, sovereign governance partial-derivative suites, non-circular 0–1 binary mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) tariff disaggregation optimization, and bilevel port network interdiction with Monte Carlo Shapley allocation. No raw or derived datasets and no document-formatting or plotting scripts are distributed.

Author: Sezgin Tunca (Department of Business and Sustainability, University of Southern Denmark, Odense, Denmark; ORCID: 0000-0001-6840-1466).
